t: LeetCode 1809 - Ad-Free Sessions: Anti-Joining Ads Out of Playback
o: Each Playback row is a time interval (inclusive on both ends) during which one customer watched, and each Ads row is a single delivery to a customer at one timestamp. An ad lands in a session when the customer matches and start_time <= timestamp <= end_time. In the example, ad 1 (customer 1, time 5) lands in session 1 ([1,5]) and ads 2 and 3 land in session 4 ([17,28]); every other session receives nothing, so sessions 2, 3 and 5 are reported. Structurally this is an anti-join: keep exactly the sessions for which no matching ad row exists. Because intervals are inclusive, both endpoints must be tested, which BETWEEN expresses directly.
k: This is an anti-join: report left-table rows that have no matching right-table row.
Sessions match ads on customer_id AND the timestamp range, never on session_id.
The interval is inclusive, so a timestamp equal to start_time or end_time still counts as shown.

a.i: Outer-join every session to all ads of the same customer that fall inside its interval. Sessions with no such ad keep NULLs in every Ads column, so filtering on a.ad_id IS NULL leaves exactly the ad-free sessions. This is the canonical pattern for rows of A with no related B.
s: LEFT JOIN Playback p to Ads a ON a.customer_id = p.customer_id AND a.timestamp BETWEEN p.start_time AND p.end_time

c.python:
# Database problem - the accepted submission is a single MySQL query:
SELECT p.session_id
FROM Playback p
LEFT JOIN Ads a
       ON a.customer_id = p.customer_id
      AND a.timestamp BETWEEN p.start_time AND p.end_time
WHERE a.ad_id IS NULL;

a.t: O(S x A) worst case - each session may probe many ads - though indexes on customer_id make it near-linear in practice.
a.sp: O(S + A) for the joined intermediate result.

a.i: Ask the question literally: keep a session only if no ad of the same customer lies inside its interval. NOT EXISTS stops scanning at the first match and sidesteps any reasoning about NULL comparison semantics.
s: For each Playback row evaluate EXISTS over Ads matching customer and interval

c.python:
# Database problem - the accepted submission is a single MySQL query:
SELECT p.session_id
FROM Playback p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM Ads a
    WHERE a.customer_id = p.customer_id
      AND a.timestamp BETWEEN p.start_time AND p.end_time
);

a.sp: O(1) beyond input - no wide intermediate join rows are materialized.

w: Either query is a strong interview answer; open with LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL and mention NOT EXISTS as the intent-revealing alternative. Pitfalls: joining on customer_id alone (ignoring time), strict inequalities instead of the inclusive interval, or accidentally writing INNER JOIN, which returns the opposite of what is asked. Follow-up: report each session with its number of ads - switch to a LEFT JOIN with COUNT(a.ad_id) grouped by session.
